speaker: Doctor
text: Since you haven't provided the patient's initial response yet, I will begin the interview. How long have you been experiencing these double vision, stair-climbing difficulty, and upper limb weakness symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the fluctuating nature of your weakness and the specific trigger for your diplopia are very helpful. To narrow this down, does swallowing food or liquids feel difficult or cause choking?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.
